answer: A decommissioned fort keeps one relic cannon per agent, and each agent fires it once a day when the sun stands at its zenith. The shot sends a white plume over the wall, and two neighbors photograph the plume with the day's date chalked on the fort gate. A cannon fired late, or a plume with no photo, costs the agent the post for a season. Faking a thousand agents means buying a thousand relic cannons and firing each one at noon every day, which costs more than any one of them earns.
